claims.text: A predictive approach incorporating descriptors of lattice distortion and force-constant fluctuations will predict low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys more accurately than methods using only averaged properties.
FeCoCrMnNi-like high-entropy alloys can be single-phase and compositionally random while exhibiting severe lattice distortion.
The expanded predictive method transforms raw compositional data into descriptors of local lattice distortion and force-constant fluctuation magnitude.
The proposed tests are restricted to temperatures at which the alloy remains single-phase and phonons dominate heat transport.
Force-constant fluctuations in FeCoCrMnNi-like random alloys are approximately 20–50%.
Intrinsic chemical randomness in high-entropy alloys gives rise to atomic-scale lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations.
Lattice distortion and force-constant fluctuations enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by lattice distortion reduces lattice thermal conductivity.
Including lattice-distortion and force-constant descriptors enables the predictive method to capture phonon scattering better than models based on averaged structural features.
The proposed approach will identify high-entropy alloys having lower phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 10–20% relative to traditional methods.
Current methods based on average atomic properties or binary-alloy analogues have broader error margins and less accurate lattice-thermal-conductivity estimates for high-entropy alloys.
The approach is primarily applicable to single-phase, statistically random high-entropy alloys.
The approach may not apply to multiphase high-entropy alloys.
The approach may not apply when electronic heat conduction dominates.
The magnitude of the predicted accuracy improvement cannot be established without benchmarking across multiple high-entropy-alloy systems.
Inelastic neutron scattering or Raman spectroscopy can be used in the proposed benchmark to measure phonon dispersion.
Laser-flash analysis can provide the lattice thermal conductivity needed for the proposed benchmark.
